newsitem.title: USA: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen off after jobs data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - US stocks seen off after jobs data.

text.p: U.S. stocks were seen moving lower after stronger-than-expected December employment data, analysts said. The following are their comments:
JIM PIZZO, SENIOR INVESTMENT STRATEGIST AT OPPENHEIMER & CO:
-- "At first blush, they certainly don't look good for the bond and stock markets. Looking at the futures now, you're going to have at least a 50-point down opening."

The U.S. Labor Department said the economy created 262,000 new jobs in December, after a revised 127,000-job gain in November. Experts in a Reuters survey had expected 192,000 new jobs to be created in December.
PIERRE ELLIS, SENIOR ECONOMIST, LEHMAN BROTHERS:
-- "For the bond market, probably for all the domestic markets, it's bad news. Over the course of the past two months wages are up 1.3 percent, which is quite an acceleration and quite threatening."
The benchmark 30-year bond fell 1-16/32 to yield 6.87 percent in reaction to the jobs data.
PHIL ORLANDO, CHIEF INVESTMENT OFFICER, VALUE LINE ASSET MANAGEMENT DIVISION:

-- "Our worst fears are met. This number is ugly and the bonds are reacting appropriately....Given the importance of this number and the implication for the upcoming FOMC (Federal Open Market Committee) meeting on February 4...weakness (in bonds) could extend up to about the seven-percent level."

-- "Given the collapse in (the) Japan (markets) overnight and weakness we saw in the bonds based on this number, and the fact that we're at another record, up around the 6600 (Dow) level, it would not surprise me to see some profit taking here today."
